q: A CW-complex is built by attaching cells. The cellular chain complex C_n = H_n(X^n, X^{n-1}) (relative homology of skeleta) has boundary maps d_n: C_n → C_{n-1} given by the degrees of attaching maps. The homology of this chain complex:
opts: Is always the same as singular homology
Equals singular homology H_*(X) (cellular homology theorem)
Depends on the CW structure chosen
exp: Cellular homology theorem: the homology of the cellular chain complex equals the singular homology of X. This gives a practical computational tool: the cellular boundary map has matrix entries given by degrees of compositions of attaching and projection maps, often computable from geometric data.
